notes: USD per unit for bought items. Made items have no price of their own: their cost comes from bom/materials.json. Path says how the item is obtained: buy_retail (retail or marketplace price), buy_bulk (distributor price), buy_used, buy_service (fabrication service), make (computed from materials), owned or salvage. checked is the date the price was seen on its source (YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY-MM, or YYYY). Empty means the source shows no date, so the price is stale until re-checked. Placeholders are guesses. Unpriced items count as $0.

items.name: Holybro Pix32 v6 autopilot (new)
items.note: Holybro on 2026-10-27: $189.00 to $252.97 depending on the kit. The Unmanned RC page listed before is gone.

items.name: Holybro Pix32 v5 (used, tested)
items.note: One used listing, undated. eBay blocked automated reading on 2026-10-27, so it was not re-checked. Crash and flight history unknown. Holybro lists the v5 as discontinued.

items.name: Holybro M9N GPS for the autopilot
items.note: Holybro $54.99 and 3DR $74.90 (with compass, shipping in 5 to 7 weeks) on 2026-10-27. Holybro points to a newer V2 model.

items.name: 2207 brushless motor, known brand (one of four)
items.note: On 2026-10-27 the T-Motor V2207 V2 was sold out at Pyrodrone ($16.99), and T-Motor's own store blocked automated reading. In stock: EMAX E3 2207 at $14.99 (WREKD) and $17.99 (RaceDayQuads). Budget eBay listings ($10 before, undated) were not re-read.

items.name: 4-in-1 ESC, 30 to 45 A class (retail)
items.note: Not priced. A single 40 A ESC was $13.82 at Walmart (old listing), so four separate ESCs would cost about $55. Guess only.

items.name: 5-inch propeller set (4-pack, retail)
items.note: RaceDayQuads on 2026-10-27: 5-inch 4-packs in stock from $2.99 to $4.99. Factory listings were $0.70 to $1.20 per prop at 4 to 100-piece minimums (an older page, not re-read), so retail is near factory price. Props are safety-critical: buy, do not make.

items.name: Commercial 5-inch frame
items.note: Not priced. Replaced by a printed frame in pass 2. Guess only.

items.name: Printed frame (PETG), from materials
items.note: Assumes 150 g of PETG, plus 20 percent waste on the high end. The PETG price is a placeholder until searched. Measure the real grams in the slicer.

items.name: Printed prop guards (set of four), from materials
items.note: Assumes 30 g of PETG for four guards. Estimate.

items.name: Printed camera mount, from materials
items.note: Assumes 30 g of PLA. Estimate.

items.name: Printed tag enclosure, from materials
items.note: Assumes 25 g of PLA for the tag case. Estimate.

items.name: Raspberry Pi 5, 4 GB (companion computer)
items.note: Raspberry Pi raised the 4 GB price to $70 on 2025-12-01, then by $15 on 2026-02-02 and by $25 on 2026-04-01: $110 (the sum is the agent's arithmetic; the posts give the steps). PiShop lists $110 on 2026-10-27.

items.name: Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W (video streamer or light companion)
items.note: On 2026-10-27: Raspberry Pi's page calls it a $15 computer; PiShop lists $17.25, and $20.75 with a header (out of stock). Needs a mini CSI camera cable, not priced.

items.name: Raspberry Pi Camera Module 3 (standard lens)
items.note: On 2026-10-27: Raspberry Pi's page says from $25, PiShop lists $29.25.

items.name: VL53L1X time-of-flight breakout (close range)
items.note: On 2026-10-27: M5Stack's Grove module (not a bare breakout) $8.95; the Pimoroni board at RobotShop $22.95. Dropped in pass 1 until logs show a need.

items.name: 4S 1500 mAh LiPo (one pack, bought)
items.note: Rotor Riot $26.99 and Helios RC $35.00 on 2026-10-27. The Pyrodrone page listed before is gone. Use a known brand for flight. Cheap unbranded packs are a fire risk. Some 15.2 V HV packs need a matching charger and ESC. Packs are not made at home.

items.name: 4S balance charger (retail)
items.note: Not priced. Guess only.

items.name: LiPo charging and storage bag
items.note: Not priced. Guess only.

items.name: ExpressLRS 2.4 GHz nano receiver (manual override link)
items.note: RadioMaster on 2026-10-27: XR2 Nano $9.99, RP1 and RP2 V2 nano receivers $18.99. The unbranded Walmart nano ($13.62 before) was not re-read. It needs a transmitter, and the kill path is only trusted after bench tests.

items.name: ExpressLRS-compatible transmitter (retail)
items.note: Not priced in research. Owning one already makes this $0. Guess only. Pass 8 replaces it with a made transmitter.

items.name: Heltec HT-CT62 (ESP32-C3 plus SX1262 LoRa node), retail
items.note: On 2026-10-27: Heltec's store $6.90, odlstore $9.00. Compare the bulk ESP32-C3 module below. Check the frequency variant for your region (915 MHz in the US).

items.name: NEO-M9N-00B bare GNSS module (tag)
items.note: LCSC on 2026-10-27: $16.55 for one, $16.15 at ten, 515 in stock. Symmetry's page now redirects to Braemac, which blocked automated reading, so its $10.99 at ten (undated) was not re-checked. Needs a carrier board. Largest chip in the tag. A clone GNSS chip is listed below as a cheaper option to test.

items.name: GNSS antenna and carrier board (tag, retail)
items.note: Not priced. The bare module needs an antenna and a carrier. Replaced by an own-design patch board in pass 7 (unverified). Guess only.

items.name: Tag battery and charge board (retail)
items.note: Not priced. Guess only. Pass 8 replaces it with a made tag battery.

items.name: ESP32-C3-MINI-1 module (bulk, distributor)
items.note: LCSC page fetched 2026-10-10: $3.06 for one piece and $2.01 at 1,300 pieces, 3,563 in stock. The page has no price date. DigiKey lists the -1U-H4 at $3.50, undated. Its Wi-Fi can link the tag to the drone, which replaces the LoRa chip in the retail module.

items.name: 2-layer PCB, 10 x 10 cm, one board (outsourced, low-markup fab)
items.note: JLCPCB's homepage on 2026-10-27: from $2.00 for 5 boards. Shipping is extra and was not checked (one user once reported $3.50 for five with shipping, undated). Only one fab is listed, so this is a single-source buy.

items.name: Passives and connectors for the tag (bulk)
items.note: Resistors, capacitors and a battery connector, bought in bulk. Not searched. Estimate only.

items.name: GNSS patch antenna on a 2-layer board (own design, unverified)
items.note: Unverified design: a GNSS patch on a 10 x 10 cm 2-layer board, priced as the bare board. Patch size and tuning are not checked. The u.FL connector is not priced. Measure the satellite signal (C/N0) on the chip before trusting it.

items.name: ATGM336H clone GNSS chip (tag, cheaper option to test)
items.note: Clone-family GNSS chip. LCSC on 2026-10-27: $3.27 for one and $1.83 at 1,000 or more, 6,888 in stock. Lower performance than u-blox, untested here. Optional until tested against the M9N.

items.name: Tag board etched in-house, 100 cm2, single-sided (comparison)
items.note: Single-sided only, for comparison with the outsourced 2-layer board. The etchant figure is conservative because ferric chloride can be reused. Per board it costs more than an outsourced 2-layer board, so in-house etching is for fast iteration, not savings.

items.name: Phone with GNSS, IMU and Wi-Fi (already owned)
items.note: Counted at $0 because you already own it. A new phone is not in the budget.

items.name: Google Pixel 8a, used (purchased by the owner)
items.note: Bought used for $250, as an example of a cheap used feature-rich phone. It is a parts source too: GNSS, IMU, camera, Wi-Fi and a cell. Not decided as a drone computer. Its battery is a fire and crash hazard on a drone.

items.name: USB-to-serial adapter (phone to autopilot link)
items.note: Not priced. Guess only.

items.name: DJI Tello, refurbished (indoor bench test platform)
items.note: Optional. DJI NYC lists $79.00 on 2026-10-27; Drone Nerds no longer lists the Tello. Indoors only, no GPS. Only for testing follow logic on a real airframe indoors, never outdoors near people.

items.name: Thrust stand for motor tests (printed base, arm and mount)
items.note: Assumes 80 g of PLA. Pair with the load cell below. Measure real thrust before trusting any motor result.

items.name: 1 kg load cell with HX711 amplifier (set)
items.note: On 2026-10-27: Adafruit's 1 kg bar load cell $3.95, with Adafruit's HX711 board ($9.95) or M5Stack's HX711 unit ($3.50). Generic sets on eBay and Walmart ($2.80 to $8.19 before, undated) block automated reading and were not re-checked. Check the capacity against the expected thrust.

items.name: DIY outrunner motor, 2207 class (one of four), retail-material route
items.note: Per motor: 40 g of 0.3 mm wire, 14 N52 discs bought per disc from a distributor, two miniature 4 x 9 x 4 mm bearings at retail, one shaft, a 25 g electrical-steel stator core cut by a fiber laser or a service, and a 30 g printed bell for the test stand. Magnets and bearings are the largest costs.

items.name: DIY outrunner motor, 2207 class (one of four), by-weight and salvage target
items.note: Target route, not yet available. Magnets bought by weight (about 16.5 g per motor, 14 discs of about 1.2 g each), wire and shaft salvaged (costed at $0), factory miniature bearings, laser-cut stator. Needs a magnet quote and a salvage check before it is real.

items.name: Desktop CNC mill, 3018 class (PCB milling, capital)
items.note: SainSmart's own store lists the Genmitsu 3018-PRO kit at $169.00 on 2026-10-27. The Amazon and eBay pages were not re-read; unbranded 3018 kits were about $115 before, undated. Capital cost, so optional. FAU or IEEE may already have one.

items.name: ICM-42688-P IMU chip (for an own autopilot board)
items.note: Reel price from DigiKey's 5,000 tier (undated) to $6.50 for one piece (reseller guide dated 2026-08-23). Lead times of 45 to 53 weeks at DigiKey and Mouser. Optional until the own autopilot board is chosen.

items.name: STM32H743VIT6 MCU (for an own autopilot board)
items.note: LCSC on 2026-10-27: $10.78 for one, $7.86 at 100, 120 in stock. Findchips was not re-read. The old $5.90 to $9.38 (a supplier guide and DigiKey) was undated. Optional until the own autopilot board is chosen.

items.name: SX1262 LoRa module (alternative tag link, not used in v0)
items.note: LoRa module, not a bare chip. On 2026-10-27: the module maker lists $4.10 at a 1,000-piece minimum, and Waveshare's Core1262-868M is $7.99 for one. Only needed if Wi-Fi range fails in the field. The bare SX1262 is not verified for 2026.

items.name: RTL-SDR Blog V4 dongle (software GNSS experiment)
items.note: Dongle only. The store page is about 150 days old (around May 2026) at $39.95. An eBay listing at $44.95 is about 44 days old (around August 2026). Receive-only.

items.name: GPS L1 low-noise amplifier with filter (software GNSS experiment)
items.note: GPIO on 2026-10-27: the 23 dB filtered L1 amplifier at $93, and filtered L1 amplifiers with an output bias tee or DC pass-through at $99. Costs more than a bulk GNSS chip, so this route is for owning the signal processing, not for saving money.

items.name: Tag battery, own (one protected cell and a charge board)
items.note: Uses an unprotected 18650 with a TP4056 DW01A module. Use only new cells from a known supplier, and test them. Not for the drone.

items.name: 4-in-1 ESC, own design (AM32-supported MCU)
items.note: Hand-assembled. Four MCUs, 24 MOSFETs (six per motor), four FD6288Q three-phase gate drivers, one 4-layer board. The MOSFET price is a placeholder, and its high end is retail. Bench tests at low voltage and a current limit before any LiPo.

items.name: Autopilot board, own design (STM32H743 and ICM-42688-P)
items.note: Not costed: barometer, magnetometer, voltage regulators, SD card, connectors. Firmware is a PX4 or ArduPilot board port (engineering time, not costed). GNSS is separate. Not flown until simulation and bench tests pass.

items.name: Transmitter, own design (ELRS-style 2.4 GHz, printed case)
items.note: Check that the chosen MCU is supported by the ELRS or EdgeTX firmware before ordering. Gimbal pots are placeholders. Needs a regulatory check for 2.4 GHz output and a field range test. The kill path must be tested before any flight.

items.name: DIY outrunner, 2207 class (one of four): factory magnets and bearings, lab-etched stator
items.note: Magnets and bearings bought from factories at their minimum orders (1,000 magnets, 100 bearings). Stator laminations photo-etched in the lab (unverified). A printed bell for the thrust stand only: a flight motor needs a metal bell, which is not priced.

items.name: DIY outrunner, 2207 class (one of four): factory magnets, bearings and stator cores
items.note: Like the lab-etched motor, but with factory stator cores at a 1,000-piece minimum. Cheap per unit, about $1,000 to $2,000 of cash to start, and it needs a drawing and new tooling.

items.name: 4-in-1 ESC, own design, factory-assembled (Economic PCBA)
items.note: The owner's design, assembled by the board factory from parts in its own stock. Assumes five boards per order (a fifth of the fixed fee each), about 600 solder joints, and three extended part types. The MOSFET price is still a placeholder. Bench tests first.

items.name: Autopilot board, own design, factory-assembled
items.note: Factory assembly suits the fine-pitch MCU and the LGA IMU, which are hard to solder by hand. About 300 joints assumed. Not costed: barometer, magnetometer, regulators, SD card, and the firmware port.

items.name: GNSS board, own design, factory-assembled (u-blox M9N)
items.note: Replaces the Holybro M9N board. No compass (not priced). The antenna is a placeholder.

items.name: Tag board v2, own design, factory-assembled (CH592 BLE and ATGM336H GNSS)
items.note: BLE replaces Wi-Fi, so the drone needs a BLE receiver (the Pi Zero 2 W has one). The clone GNSS module is untested, and BLE range must be measured in the field. If either fails, fall back to the ESP32 and M9N tag.

items.name: Import duty and entry fees for factory orders (allowance)
items.note: The US small-parcel exemption ended for China in May 2025, so factory orders pay duty and entry fees. Sources disagree on the 2026 rate. Guess only. Consolidate orders into one entry, or share a group order through the IEEE club.

items.name: Desktop filament extruder kit (pellets to filament, capital)
items.note: Felfil Evo kit EUR 699, or EUR 1,399 with a spooler, converted at an assumed 1.10 USD per EUR. Pellets at $1 to $4.85 per kg against filament at $8.55 to $18 means it pays back only after roughly 55 to 150 kg. Not worth it at hobby scale unless a lab already has one.

items.name: Wearable IMU board (per unit, for later companion tiers)
items.note: Not priced. Only needed if the tiers reach wearable IMUs. Costs add up quickly per unit.
